label: Счёт
description: A 10-sentence usage card for счёт (bill; account).

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Счёт' is a masculine noun in the nominative as the subject, here meaning the restaurant bill. 'На столе' locates it, and 'уже' adds immediacy.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Счёт' is the accusative direct object of 'принесите'; inanimate masculine nouns keep the nominative form. A standard polite request in a café.
Strategic focus: Genitive of absence. 'Счёта' is the genitive after the negated 'нет', meaning no account exists. 'Банковского' agrees in the masculine genitive. The ё is kept in the inflected form.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'Счёте' is the prepositional form after 'на', locating the money in the account. 'Деньги' is the plural subject, and 'уже' adds immediacy.
Strategic focus: Dative after preposition. 'Счёту' is the dative form after 'по', meaning paid according to the bill. 'Вовремя' confirms it was on time. A common payment phrase.

Strategic focus: Instrumental of means. 'Счётом' is the instrumental expressing the means of settling, keeping the ё. 'Наличным' agrees in the masculine instrumental. It pairs with the verb 'расплатился'.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'Счёте' is the prepositional after 'о', here meaning the score of a match, a second sense of счёт. 'Матча' is the genitive specifying which game.
Strategic focus: Accusative object with a dative. 'Счёт' is the accusative direct object of 'принёс', while 'нам' is the dative recipient. A clean restaurant-scene sentence.

Strategic focus: Nominative plural. 'Счета' is the nominative plural subject, with the stressed -а ending typical of this noun. 'Все' agrees in the plural, and 'оплачены' is the short passive predicate.
Strategic focus: Accusative plural. 'Счета' is the accusative plural object of 'проверяю'; inanimate plurals match the nominative plural. 'Свои' agrees in the plural, marking the speaker's own bills.
